newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - More moisture hits HRW areas.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - More moisture hits HRW areas.

text.p: More moisture fell Tuesday night and Wednesday morning across a large swath of the hard red winter wheat belt, further easing concerns about dry soil conditions, grain merchandisers said.
"It's wet, overcast, foggy," a dealer in north central Oklahoma said. "The whole state is back to above normal (moisture levels). We're pretty wet now."

Meteorology firm Weather Express, in its daily precipitation forecast map, said two to four inches of snow were likely to fall in western Kansas, eastern Colorado and the Oklahoma Panhandle, with heavier amounts to the east.

Meanwhile, basis bids for HRW wheat were steady to weaker Wednesday in response to the increase in sales of both new and old crop hard red winter wheat Monday, merchandisers said. Movement was said to have slowed from Monday's level.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: H=KCBT March wheat futures. K=KCBT May wheat futures.
